aboutH2: Michael Walsh: Addiction Counselling and Mental Health Therapy in Victoria, BC
intro: Michael and his team help empower individuals and families across Canada and throughout the world to overcome substance use, addiction, and mental health challenges. Our compassionate, expert-led services provide personalized support for lasting recovery, delivered through secure tele-therapy, online video and some in-person options.

To be clear about what this listing is: Michael Walsh is an individual addictions specialist with a small team of recovery coaches, sober companions and clinicians, not a residential treatment centre. He trades as Sober Coach Canada, and his practice offers recovery coaching, counselling, family support and planned interventions. There are no beds and no detox. Most work happens by video or phone, with in-person sessions at his offices in Victoria, Duncan and Vancouver.

pillars.title: Online First, With Offices on Vancouver Island and in Vancouver
pillars.body: Most clients never come to an office. Sessions run by video, phone, text and email, so people in Victoria, the Cowichan Valley, Nanaimo and the rest of Canada work with the team the same way. When meeting face to face helps, there are offices on Shelbourne Street in Victoria, on Kenneth Street in Duncan and on Mainland Street in Vancouver's Yaletown. Interventions in Victoria and Vancouver are done in person, and a sober companion can come to your home or travel with you.

pillars.title: Support After Detox or Rehab
pillars.body: A lot of Michael's clients come to him straight out of detox or an inpatient program, and coaching is set up to carry that work into daily life. The practice suggests weekly 60-minute sessions for the first four to six weeks, then 30-minute check-ins every two weeks. Some people stay three to six months, others a year or two. For the riskiest stretch, a sober companion can live in for a few months after treatment. Families can keep going with CRAFT coaching once their loved one is home.

pillars.title: A Coach Who Has Been Through It
pillars.body: Michael Walsh went through alcohol detox twice and inpatient drug rehab twice before he got well, and he is open about it. He has now spent about 15 years working in substance use and mental health, including jobs with the Victoria Cool Aid Society and with Island Health at its Sobering Centre, community medical detox and The Grove men's sober living residence. He trained as a recovery coach and as an interventionist, co-created the online program Home Based Recovery, and is a founding member of Recovery Coaches Canada. Every coach on his team has lived experience too.

overviewH2: Our Addiction and Mental Health Services
overview: Sober Coaching: One-on-one guidance and accountability for those in early recovery or post-rehab, helping you stay on track and working toward your goals for change and growth.
Addiction Recovery Coaching: Tailored approach for those who are sober curious wanting to reduce intake or take a break from consuming alcohol.
Intervention Services: Support for families to lovingly guide a loved one toward treatment with empathy and clarity.
Family Support: Resources and counselling using the CRAFT Model of Addiction to help families navigate addiction’s impact together.
Assessments: Comprehensive psychological, substance use, and mental health evaluations to inform your recovery plan.

Online Addiction Treatment: Do rehab online at home with Home Based Recovery providing psycho-educational and skills-building content while matched up with a recovery coach or therapist for 20-hours of support in our 30-day program.

location.heading: Michael Walsh, Addictions Specialist in Victoria, British Columbia
location.intro: Michael Walsh's main office is on Shelbourne Street in Victoria, on southern Vancouver Island, and he also sees clients at offices in Duncan in the Cowichan Valley and on Mainland Street in Vancouver. From Vancouver to the Victoria office takes about three hours with the BC Ferries crossing from Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay; Duncan is about 50 minutes north of Victoria over the Malahat, Langford about 20 minutes and Nanaimo about an hour and 45 minutes. Most sessions are online, so you can work with him from anywhere in BC or Canada.

faqIntro: Answers come from the original listing and Michael Walsh's own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Michael Walsh a rehab centre?
faqs.a: No. Michael Walsh is an individual addictions specialist and recovery coach who works with a small team under the name Sober Coach Canada. The practice offers coaching, counselling, family support, interventions and sober companions, mostly online, with offices in Victoria, Duncan and Vancouver. It has no beds and does not provide detox or residential treatment.

faqs.q: How much does recovery coaching with Michael Walsh cost?
faqs.a: Coaching is sold in six-hour blocks that cost $500 to $900, depending on the coach, according to the practice's own FAQ. You use the block through scheduled 30 or 60 minute sessions. The first consultation by phone or video is free, and sober companion rates are quoted separately.

faqs.q: How long does recovery coaching last?
faqs.a: Some clients use coaching for three to six months, others for six to twelve months, and some for two years or more. A common start is weekly 60-minute sessions for four to six weeks, then 30-minute sessions every two weeks. The schedule is set around your needs.

No, the practice does not provide medical detox. If you need it, the team can help you weigh detox and treatment programs and plan your next steps, and coaching often starts right after someone leaves detox or rehab.

His main office is at 3066 Shelbourne Street, Suite 245, in Victoria. There is also an office at 177 Kenneth Street in Duncan, in the Cowichan Valley, and one at 500-1122 Mainland Street in Vancouver. Most sessions happen by video or phone, so you do not need to live near an office.

faqs.q: Can families get help, or arrange an intervention?
faqs.a: Yes. Families can book CRAFT-based coaching to learn how to support a loved one, or plan an invitational intervention, which the practice runs in person in Victoria and Vancouver. It also runs Interventions.ca for this work.

faqs.q: Can I use my benefits to pay for coaching?
faqs.a: Usually not. Recovery coaching is not normally covered by extended health plans, though some insurers have covered it for clients, and the practice cannot bill insurers directly. It is private pay, and Michael can talk through how to approach your benefits provider.
Michael Walsh offers addiction counselling, mental health therapy, quit drinking coaching, and personalized online alcohol treatment programs.

faqs.q: How does the online alcohol treatment program work?
faqs.a: Michael Walsh’s online alcohol treatment provides flexible, confidential support tailored to your needs, with coaching sessions conducted virtually.

faqs.q: Is Michael Walsh’s counselling approach personalized?
faqs.a: Yes. Michael creates customized plans based on each client’s unique situation, ensuring compassionate and effective addiction recovery support.

faqs.q: Who can benefit from Michael Walsh’s quit drinking coaching?
faqs.a: Anyone seeking to regain control over alcohol use, whether looking to cut back or quit entirely, can benefit from Michael’s expert guidance.

faqs.q: Do I have to want to quit drinking completely?
faqs.a: No. Coaching is not built around abstinence, so you can work toward cutting back, taking a break or quitting. You set the goals and the pace with your coach.
